name: TYT TH-9800
notes: Quad-band (10 m / 6 m / 2 m / 70 cm) FM mobile, 50 W on VHF, an FT-8900 workalike. NOT BENCH-VERIFIED: every number below is read out of the CHIRP driver source (chirp/drivers/th9800.py, upstream), not off a physical radio, which is the difference between this entry and yaesu_ft2800m. Treat it as paper-derived until someone clones a real TH-9800. The driver itself is registered as an ExperimentalRadio and its own get_prompts() warns that support is 'still under development' and tells the operator to keep an OEM backup, so that warning is inherited by anything codeplugger emits here. Storage limits are the driver's: max_channels 800 is memory_bounds (1, 800); max_channel_name_chars 6 is valid_name_length = 6, as tight as the FT-270R and FT-2800M, so display names need aggressive shortening, and the charset is CHARSET_UPPER_NUMERIC plus '#*-+', i.e. upper case, digits, space and those four symbols only, with no lower case (verified against the live driver registry 2026-09-29, valid_characters = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ 1234567890#*-+'). max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim because the driver sets has_bank = False. modes is ['FM', 'AM']: the driver's valid_modes is ['WFM', 'FM', 'NFM', 'AM'], and the capabilities schema has no WFM/NFM tokens, so the wide and narrow FM variants collapse into FM and bandwidths_khz 25.0/12.5 carries that split instead. WFM is broadcast-width receive only and has no bandwidths_khz entry; AM is receive only (airband), which is why the table renders it 'AM RX'. TX BANDS ARE DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN THE DRIVER'S valid_bands, and this is the part to read before trusting the file. The driver's valid_bands (26-33, 47-54, 108-180, 220-260, 350-399.995, 400-512, 750-950 MHz) is the programming span the CHIRP UI will let you type into, not an authorization to transmit, and the TH-9800 is widely sold with wide TX open from the factory. The radio does not take its transmit limits from the driver at all: th9800.py declares struct bandlimits[9] (lorx/hirx/lotx/hitx per band, over BANDS = 30/50/60/108/150/250/350/450/850 MHz) inside the codeplug image, and get_settings() surfaces all four edges under 'Model Info' with set_mutable(False) -- CHIRP displays them and refuses to change them. Transmit range is therefore a per-unit, per-region fact baked into the image, so this file will not assert it. The four TX bands recorded here are the US amateur allocations the radio is sold to cover (28.0-29.7, 50-54, 144-148, 430-450 MHz); every driver span is additionally recorded as rx_only, overlapping those TX bands the same way yaesu_ft2800m overlaps its 137-174 MHz receive span. OPERATORS SHOULD READ THEIR OWN RADIO: open the CHIRP settings tab, Model Info, and compare the per-band Tx Start / Tx end values against these bands before assuming a channel outside them will key. A unit whose bandlimits genuinely open up MARS/CAP-style coverage is a separate id, following the yaesu_ft2800m / yaesu_ft2800m_mars split, and it should be added only from a real clone image rather than from a product listing. MODEL STRING IS AMBIGUOUS AND MATTERS FOR WRITES: TYT shipped the SAME 'TH9800' model string in the TH-7800, so the driver's match_model() cannot use it alone -- it requires a 65296-byte image AND filedata[0xfe18:0xfe1e] == b'TH9800' AND a non-zero first bandlimit block at 0xfe40:0xfe50, that last condition being the only thing separating a TH-9800 from a TH-7800. Do not relax that check, and do not assume a file that merely contains 'TH9800' belongs to this radio. Two sibling classes live in the same driver file and are NOT this entry: TYTTH9800File (MODEL 'TH-9800 File', _memsize 69632, the .dat file-backed variant) and RetevisMA1Radio (VENDOR 'Retevis', MODEL 'MA1'), which branches on MODEL == 'MA1' throughout the shared base and has a different memory format and band plan. Clone protocol is CloneModeRadio at 38400 baud, _memsize 65296 with _mmap_offset 0x0010; clone_mode is recorded as manual because the transfer is armed from the radio's own menu on each leg. WRITE PATH IS UNVERIFIED: no read, no write, and no read-back has been performed against hardware, so the chirp-writer path for this model is untested end to end. Take a full OEM backup before the first write to a real radio, and expect to confirm the read leg before trusting the write leg.
